My name is not important, but I farm this rented plot here in the South East. It is humid forest land, good for yam and cassava, so I plant my tubers as my fathers did. I cannot waste money on chemical fertilizer for roots — the land still gives, and I use the household manure and leaves to help the soil. I use my own seed from last year's harvest, and with my wife and children we do most of the work ourselves, though at planting and harvest I must call on two or three men to help for a few days.
